walkthroughs.body_html:
Chemistry of the Environment — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Chemistry of the Environment brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Chemistry of the Environment.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How does a catalyst speed up a reaction?
options: It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
A catalyst lowers the activation energy of the original reaction pathway.

mcqs.q: What does a mole of a substance represent?
options: Avogadro's number (6.02 x 10^23) of particles of that substance.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.
A catalyst gives extra kinetic energy to the reactant particles.
A mole is a unit of mass equal to the relative molecular mass in grams of any substance.

mcqs.q: At room temperature and pressure, what volume does 1 mole of any gas occupy?
options: Different gases occupy completely different volumes proportional to their molar mass.
Heavier gases occupy a smaller volume per mole because their particles are denser.
Approximately 24 dm^3 (24,000 cm^3), regardless of the identity of the gas.
A mole is a unit of volume equal to 24 dm^3 at any temperature.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Crude oil”?
options: Complete: alkane + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Incomplete: produces CO and soot.
Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.
Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.
Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Saturated”?
options: Contains only single C–C bonds; cannot add more atoms across a bond.
Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.
Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.
Saturated hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — all single bonds.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “First four alkanes”?
options: Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.
Saturated hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — all single bonds.
Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.
Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Hydrocarbon”?
options: Complete: alkane + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Incomplete: produces CO and soot.
Saturated hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — all single bonds.
Methane CH₄, ethane C₂H₆, propane C₃H₈, butane C₄H₁₀.
Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Alkane”?
options: Contains only single C–C bonds; cannot add more atoms across a bond.
Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.
Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.
Saturated hydrocarbon with general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ — all single bonds.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Combustion of alkanes”?
options: Mixture of hydrocarbons (mostly alkanes), separated by fractional distillation.
Compound containing only hydrogen and carbon.
Contains only single C–C bonds; cannot add more atoms across a bond.
Complete: alkane + O₂ → CO₂ + H₂O. Incomplete: produces CO and soot.
